children: The newly formed cloud company Crux AI, which is a joint venture between Google
, has secured $22B in bank loans, according to Bloomberg.

The loans will be used to acquire Google's tensor processing units, or TPUs, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. The loans will be backed by Crux AI's customer commitments and the value of the chips purchased. Banks involved in the loan included Goldman Sachs Group, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking, Barclays Plc, BNP Paribas SA, and Bank of Nova Scotia.
Crux AI plans to provide cloud compute for AI labs such as OpenAI
. It will be competing against fellow neoclouds such as CoreWeave
The company was launched just last week and plans to bring 500 MW of compute capacity online in 2027 in the first phase of its roadmap.

"AI presents a generational technological shift and, with it, the opportunity to reimagine the infrastructure powering it from the ground up," said Benjamin Treynor Sloss, CEO of Crux AI. "That is what we are building at Crux AI: an integrated platform designed end-to-end to operate reliably at enormous scale. Our ambition is to become the infrastructure company trusted with the workloads that matter most."
Sloss worked at Google for more than 20 years before launching Crux AI.

title: Google-backed neocloud Crux AI secures $22B in bank loans to support chip purchases: report
